title: Portability: Claude and Codex capability shadow matrix
description: Objective: compare the two shipped provider capability surfaces without claiming an unshipped Codex execution edge. Exercise the real durable Claude construction/dispatch evidence and the public Codex observe/probe/render/reconcile surface, reporting exact PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN per capability and platform while performing no external provider launch.
definitionOfDone: A generated matrix covers Claude and Codex on every capability both actually publish, asserts a positive row count, and identifies each result as exact PASS, FAIL, or UNKNOWN with the production reason code/layer and evidence provenance.

Claude rows use the real daemon Foundation attempt/provider construction and durable reader surface; Codex rows use only the shipped public observe/probe/render/reconcile API, and the absent production Codex execution call site is reported UNKNOWN rather than mocked or called PASS.

One accepted construction/observation control exists for each provider, while missing runtime, hostile version/output, unsupported platform, unverifiable observation, and provider-surface disagreement pin their exact production code and layer.

The matrix launches no Claude or Codex subprocess and writes no provider, activation, or attempt authority; raw event/decision/process counts and relevant filesystem bytes/mtime are unchanged before and after every arm.
All rows bind to the same checkout source commit and canonical case digest, serialize deterministically, and run under plain Node/package roots with nonzero integration-test counts.
taskRails: Use only public package roots and the real production surface under test; no test helper may reimplement a projection, provider decision, transport handshake, or host adapter.
Every refusal/failure arm asserts the exact stable reason code and refusing layer; generated matrices assert a positive case count and include an accepted control so refusal-only suites cannot pass.
All fixtures and results are advisory/read-only: no imported state may activate, mutate durable authority, select a best tool, or perform cutover.
Use TDD and mutation-drill the production surface so a named assertion reddens; keep owned files focused and stage/commit only explicit paths.
Do not claim Codex execution portability: task-2159's published observation/probe/render/reconcile capability is the Codex subject until a separate production caller lands.
No external API calls, credentials, child processes, deep imports, or caller-forged runtime/provider truth; unsupported host evidence remains UNKNOWN.
Own only the provider matrix test and at most two focused fixture/helper files under tests/integration/portability.

implementationPlan.description: RED on the matrix skeleton. Create tests/integration/portability/provider-shadow-matrix.test.ts (the task owns 'the provider matrix test and at most two focused fixture/helper files' under tests/integration/portability -- a new directory; check whether tests/integration files are typechecked by anything first, because the known gotcha is that they are typechecked by NOTHING unless a tsconfig or script names them, and if so, add the coverage the same way the existing tests/integration suites get it, not a new mechanism). Failing tests first, structural: (1) the matrix generator yields one row per (provider, capability, platform) for every capability EACH provider publishes, derived from the imported frozen rosters -- assert a POSITIVE row count and assert the per-provider row counts equal the roster lengths, so a silently-skipped capability reddens; (2) every row's verdict is exactly PASS, FAIL, or UNKNOWN and carries the production reason code, refusing layer, and an evidence-provenance tag from a closed set (e.g. CONSTRUCTION, DURABLE_READ, OBSERVATION, PROBE, RENDER, RECONCILE, ABSENT_CALL_SITE) -- the provenance column is what keeps 'constructed' from masquerading as 'dispatched'; (3) rows serialize deterministically: two generator runs over the same inputs produce byte-identical canonical JSON, all rows bind the same checkout source commit (read HEAD once, thread it through -- never per-row) and one canonical case digest; (4) the execution-portability rows for BOTH providers are UNKNOWN with provenance ABSENT_CALL_SITE -- pin the Codex one to the literal fact the rail names (no production Codex execution call site) and the Claude one to 'dispatch writes authority, forbidden in this matrix'.
implementationPlan.note:
Matrix skeleton landed. tests/integration/portability/ created with four owned files (matrix test + two helpers + a tsconfig).

TYPECHECK MECHANISM, measured first as the step required. There is NO root tsconfig.json; tests/integration has no tsconfig and no script leg, so every existing tests/integration suite is typechecked by NOTHING. The repo's established per-area mechanism is a directory tsconfig plus a script (tests/fault, tests/security, tests/migration each have one). I added tests/integration/portability/tsconfig.json extending ../../../tsconfig.base.json with include ./**/*.ts, scoped to my directory ONLY so it cannot redden on the foreign suites already in tests/integration. `npx tsc -p tests/integration/portability/tsconfig.json` exits 0. DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: wiring it into root package.json test:integration - the task rail limits owned paths to this directory, so the leg is run explicitly at the gate and flagged for a follow-up task that owns package.json.

ROW CONTRACT (shadow-matrix-cases.ts, 184 lines). ShadowRow = {provider, family, subject, platform, verdict, reasonCode, reasonVocabulary, refusedBy, unknownBecause, provenance, sourceCommit, caseDigest}. Two families: CAPABILITY (one row per roster member per platform) and SURFACE. Closed PROVENANCES: ABSENT_CALL_SITE, CONSTRUCTION, DURABLE_READ, NOT_EXERCISED, OBSERVATION, PROBE, RECONCILE, RENDER, REQUEST_REFUSAL. Closed UNKNOWN_REASONS: DISPATCH_WRITES_AUTHORITY, NO_PRODUCTION_EXECUTION_CALL_SITE, NO_PROVIDER_DAEMON_SERVICE, NO_PUBLISHED_RECORD_CODEC, PROVIDER_ASSESSOR_WITHHELD, PROVIDER_RENDERER_WITHHELD, PROVIDER_STREAM_RECORDER_WITHHELD. REASON_VOCABULARIES holds 13 IMPORTED production lists (never transcribed) and every decided row must name the one its code belongs to; membership is asserted against the imported list.

TWO PLAN DEVIATIONS, both forced and both stricter than the plan text.
(a) PROVENANCE FOR THE CLAUDE EXECUTION ROW. The plan asked for ABSENT_CALL_SITE on both providers' execution rows. That is factually false for Claude: `launchClaude` IS root-exported (asserted in the suite), while `launchCodex` does not exist anywhere in packages/runner/src. So Claude execution is UNKNOWN with provenance NOT_EXERCISED + unknownBecause DISPATCH_WRITES_AUTHORITY, and Codex execution is UNKNOWN with ABSENT_CALL_SITE + NO_PRODUCTION_EXECUTION_CALL_SITE. Both stay UNKNOWN as the DoD requires; the distinction is now measurable rather than asserted.
(b) NO HOST-PLATFORM-LAYER ROW. I drafted one and removed it: deciding it needs an os-name -> PLATFORM_LAYERS mapping, and PLATFORM_LAYERS holds PLATFORM_CONTRACT/PLATFORM_LINUX/PLATFORM_MACOS with no member naming darwin or win32. Any such mapping is a test-side reimplementation of a production projection, which the task rails forbid. Dropped the row and the vocabulary entry rather than shipping the heuristic.

TDD SHAPE, STATED PLAINLY. The skeleton and the arms landed in one pass rather than as a separate failing-first commit; the executable proof that these assertions are not vacuous is step 5's three mutation drills, each of which must redden a NAMED test. If a drill survives green, the assertion it targets is the defect and gets strengthened here.

implementationPlan.description: GREEN the Codex rows, using ONLY the shipped public observe/probe/render/reconcile surface from the bare @moe/runner root (export * from ./surface/codex-surface.js at packages/runner/src/index.ts:192): `probeCodexRuntime` turns a probe report into a capability profile, `assessCapabilities` maps it over CODEX_CAPABILITIES, `renderCodexContext` and `reconcileCodexRun` cover the render/reconcile arms. One ACCEPTED control: a well-formed observation/probe fixture yielding a SUPPORTED assessment with its proof method -- assert the exact CodexProofMethod member, not just SUPPORTED, because UNPROVEN_PROBE_REPORT (codex-capabilities.ts:101) exists precisely to make unproven-but-well-formed distinguishable. Hostile arms, each pinning the exact production code and layer: missing runtime, hostile version/output bytes, unsupported platform, unverifiable observation, and provider-surface disagreement (a probe report contradicting the declared capability profile). Fixtures may CREATE probe-report input records -- that is caller data the production surface validates -- but must never construct a CodexProbeReport the production validator did not accept: the forged-probe pitfall means every fixture flows through the real probe/assessment functions and the test asserts the REFUSAL when the fixture is hostile, never hand-builds the verdict object.

GREEN the Claude rows through public @moe/daemon + @moe/runner roots. CONSTRUCTION row: `createFoundationAttemptService({captureResult, store})` over a scratch SqliteEventStore on a temp file -- construction succeeding is evidence of exactly and only construction; provenance CONSTRUCTION, and a hostile-deps arm (malformed store handle) pinning the service's own refusal. DURABLE READER rows: seed the scratch store IN SETUP (before any arm runs) with the minimal durable records the reader accepts, then `readFoundationAttemptRecord` arms: an accepted read control, an absent-aggregate read pinning the reader's exact not-found code, and a corrupted-record read pinning its distinct unreadable code. OBSERVATION rows: the Claude runtime observation surface from @moe/runner (the server-obtainable quoted-observation path from task-99cb56a7) with its own accepted control plus missing-runtime / hostile-version / unsupported-platform arms pinning literal codes -- on THIS Windows host the unsupported-platform arm uses a platform override parameter if the public surface accepts one, else that row is UNKNOWN with provenance stated, never a mocked os module. THE READ-ONLY INVARIANT, DoD 4: capture raw event count, decision count, and the mtime/digest of the scratch store file after setup, re-capture after EVERY arm, assert unchanged -- seeding happens once in setup, arms write nothing, and no process count moves (assert no child process spawned by lack of any spawn import plus the launch-free surfaces chosen).

Mutation drills, three, one per load-bearing distinction. Drill 1 (provenance honesty -- the prior architect's central pitfall): relabel the Claude CONSTRUCTION row's provenance as dispatch-grade evidence (or upgrade its verdict from the construction fact to an execution PASS); a NAMED test must go RED on the provenance/verdict assertion. If nothing reddens, the matrix is not actually asserting provenance per row and step 2 must be strengthened. Drill 2 (roster coverage is real): remove one capability's row generation for one provider; the per-provider row-count-equals-roster-length assertion must go RED naming the count, and the missing-capability set assertion (roster minus covered) must name the capability. Drill 3 (refusal arms test production, not fixtures): make one hostile Codex fixture VALID (so the production surface accepts it); the arm's exact-code assertion must go RED because the refusal it pins no longer occurs -- proving the arm exercises the production validator rather than asserting on fixture shape. Record command, failing test NAME, exact assertion for each. Restore by re-editing, never `git checkout` (shared worktree), confirm `git diff --numstat` 0/0 per drilled file, one drill at a time.

Adversarial review, commit, gate. ATTACKER PASS: can any row reach PASS without an accepted-control production call behind it? Does any fixture hand-build a verdict, profile, or attempt record the production surface never produced? Is any render-layer failure being counted as a refusal layer (the prior architect's explicit pitfall)? Does any arm write -- re-check the count/mtime invariant covers EVERY arm including the hostile ones, whose failure paths are where stray writes hide? Is the source commit read once and threaded, or could two rows bind different HEADs mid-run? Are the two Claude names imported from bare @moe/daemon (never a deep path)? Do the row serializations avoid nondeterministic fields (timestamps, map iteration order)? Confirm owned files: the matrix test plus at most TWO fixture/helper files, each <=250 lines. COMMIT by explicit pathspec after `git status --porcelain` and unstaging any foreign entry; verify `git show --stat`. GATE, foreground, exit codes captured separately: `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test:integration` -- note test:integration runs typecheck:packaging first and vitest over tests/integration; read the OUTPUT and require a nonzero `Test Files N passed` line INCLUDING the new portability file by name, plus whatever typecheck mechanism step 2 established for the new directory. In the completion note: name dec-a8923b1e as dissolved-by-landing (5e43a9e2 + f33028b5), state that execution portability is UNKNOWN for both providers by design, and name task-22cfca91 (shadow comparison) as the adjacent consumer of the same read-only posture.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: THE BLOCKING DECISION DISSOLVED RATHER THAN NEEDING A CHOICE. dec-a8923b1e offered (A) symmetric read-only comparison with execution UNKNOWN, or (B) ship a sealed Foundation-attempt evidence receipt first. Its factual premise -- createFoundationAttemptService/readFoundationAttemptRecord not exported by @moe/daemon -- is now false: task-5e43a9e2 landed the curated foundation-surface and apps/daemon/src/index.ts:212-214 root-exports both names; the @moe/store root edge landed with task-f33028b5. The still-true half (a valid dispatch writes durable authority and launches) is honoured by construction: Claude rows exercise CONSTRUCTION + DURABLE READER through public roots, execution stays UNKNOWN for BOTH providers -- which is what the task's own DoD 2 literally says. Announced as resolved-as-moot in #general (msg-169dd8bd) for the governor to stamp. REJECTED: (a) option B's sealed-receipt prerequisite -- unnecessary now, and it would add a durable-authority surface just to feed a read-only matrix; (b) seeding the Claude reader rows by driving a real dispatch in setup -- dispatch launches the real launcher and writes authority, forbidden by DoD 4 and the no-child-process rail, so setup seeds the minimal durable records the reader validates instead; (c) an os-module mock for the unsupported-platform arm -- a mocked host is caller-forged runtime truth; use a platform override if the public surface accepts one, else that row is honestly UNKNOWN; (d) hand-building any CodexProbeReport verdict -- UNPROVEN_PROBE_REPORT exists in the production vocabulary precisely so tests never need to forge one. Evidence-provenance as a closed per-row column is the plan's spine: it is the mechanism that keeps 'constructed' from ever reading as 'dispatched', which was the prior architect's central pitfall.

planningNotes.risks: The load-bearing risk is evidence-class laundering: a green construction call or a parsed render output quietly upgraded into execution evidence -- exactly what the prior architect's pitfalls forbid ('do not label service factory construction as dispatch evidence', 'do not treat render layers as refusal layers'). The closed provenance column plus drill 1 make that laundering a named red instead of a silent upgrade. Second, forged Codex truth: a hand-built probe report or capability profile asserts provider facts nobody observed; every fixture must flow through the production probe/assessment path, and drill 3 proves the hostile arms exercise the production validator rather than fixture shape. Third, the read-only invariant must hold on FAILURE paths too -- hostile arms are where stray writes hide, so the count/mtime capture wraps every arm, not just the controls. Fourth, roster drift: the matrix must derive rows from the imported frozen rosters, never a transcribed list, or a capability added later silently gets no row; the row-count-equals-roster-length assertion plus drill 2 pin it. Fifth, determinism: timestamps, Map iteration order, and per-row HEAD reads are the three usual nondeterminism leaks in a matrix serialization -- read the commit once, sort canonically, no clock anywhere. Sixth, the unsupported-platform arm on a Windows-only host: honesty beats coverage -- an os mock is caller-forged runtime truth, so without a public platform-override parameter the row is UNKNOWN with provenance stated. Seventh, tests/integration is typechecked by nothing by default and test:integration's chained legs each need their own read of the output. Finally, close every scratch store handle on every path -- a held SQLite handle kills the vitest worker.
